judge-football.justification: Usable (8.3): concrete rule (100+ routes and SOE above zero), named 2026 list of 13 receivers, drill protocol (slant, dagger, comeback twice). The 62% vs 19% headline pools all draft rounds; the day-3 pool the rule targets is only 6 of 12 vs 2 of 8 with an interval crossing zero. Confounders (8.8): handles opportunity and pick, route mix and depth, QB effects, Nacua leverage, drill reliability and ceiling, sampled-play limits, frozen-rule hash; scheme splits do not repeat. Weak spots: players in two season pairs, post-hoc ridge choice. Unique (8.0): same-player same-route-family drill-to-game translation with reliability ceiling is a real reframing; price-vs-value test adds. Mostly null Break G plus SOE-persistence shortlist (close to autocorrelation) dilutes the pivot. Terminology (8.2): football terms plausible, six named players with deployment splits; g force reading and 0.4 catches a season conversion slightly stretched; text-to-numbers.json mismatch (price 14% vs 9%) is a credibility risk.
top_changes: Rebuild the headline around the day-3/UDFA pool; report its hit rate vs base rate with an interval (6/12 vs 2/8). If it cannot be made firm, say so in the lede and do not quote the all-rounds 62% vs 19% as the rule's result. Add a SOE-persistence-vs-pick-forecast baseline (0.44 year-to-year correlation makes the gap partly mechanical).

Fix number consistency: reconcile 14% [5,23] price vs price_bg=9 [2,17] in numbers.json and Fig 4. Check word count with wc -w. Cut Holm, Bonferroni, ridge and QB detail; cut 5-row tests table to 3 rows.

Show a decision case where Break G and tape disagree with the shortlist outcome (extend the Boutte row to a scout action) with one clip-level cue. Replace generic role actions with route-family-specific coaching. Give 2026 shortlist names with SOE and routes in a small table, flagging soft-cut ones as test cases.

judge-datascience.justification: Ran analysis.py in a scratch repo (~5 min); all 1,017 numbers.json entries matched exactly (deterministic). Headline slope (-0.4 [-2.2,+1.7], shuffle p 0.74), 16/26 vs 5/27 shortlist, 14% price, drill reliability (rho 0.28, 0.53 rising to 0.62) and NFL-vs-drill rho -0.11 reproduced. Fisher exact not run (no scipy); p values taken from numbers.json. Strengths: no-tracking baseline (log pick, 40, weight, NGS, TE flag) with ridge, weight estimated on held-out class; leave-one-class-out with refitting player bootstrap; year- and drill-standardized scores; mixed-model reliability and ceiling; frozen hashed rule; pre-set +3 in margin, Nacua-excluded version, 70-test ledger; new 10 Hz break detector, route-family drill-to-play matching, identical-code Break G. Weaknesses: action 1 says day-3/UDFA rule right 62% vs 40% base but those are all-rounds figures (16/26); day-3 is 6/12 vs 2/8, gap [-14,58], p=0.26. Shortlist headline is SOE persistence, not tracking-derived, with overlapping pairs (53 pairs, 38 receivers); Bonferroni over ledger non-significant. Ridge main test (-0.4) adopted after plain (-1.2) seen; shuffle p moved 0.38 to 0.74; ridge calibration varies by class (0.52, 3.95, 1.86). Price lead borderline (Holm 16%), held-out R2 gain 1.4 points spanning zero. Game metric reliability 0.23 so null is underpowered and 'does not transfer' too strong. SOE not target-quality adjusted; QB share on 4,071 snaps. Decel, apex-speed, re-acceleration reliabilities 0.12, -0.04, 0.05; only G usable.
top_changes: Fix the day-3 claim in action 1: report 6/12 vs 2/8 against the 40% base (all-rounds 62% is a different pool). Add leave-one-season-out or time-forward evaluation of the shortlist rule. Cluster bootstrap/Fisher interval by receiver. Report gap net of regression to the mean (pick and routes only rule).

Pre-register ridge vs plain as one primary test or report a combined estimate. Add leave-one-class-out interval for the ridge weight. Give a Bayesian posterior or equivalence statement for Break G so the null is a bounded effect.

Raise game-side power: reliability-disattenuated drill-to-game correlation with interval; test only players with at least 8 graded NFL break reps; add target-quality-adjusted SOE as main outcome plus Nacua-free yards per route run in the headline table.

judge-writeup.justification: check.py passes (1,801 words by its count, 4 figures, 2 tables; wc -w 1,963). Lede states result and action within ~80 words: hard Combine cut gives no separation (-0.4 in, 90% interval -2.2 to +1.7), last season's separation repeats 62% vs 19%. Structure follows finalist pattern. Prior-round complaints addressed (positive use is headline, table is 5 rows, Boutte drill-vs-tape case). Weaknesses: 'The test' is a stack of bolded mini-paragraphs; 62% vs 19% from 53 pairs with repeated receivers, day-3 subset (6/12 vs 2/8) interval includes zero; lede's 62% is all-rounds but the so-what's 62% vs 40% refers to a different pool; metric paragraph has notebook detail (same code, frozen hashes); 'Why it matters' thin; shuffle p, Holm, ridge leak into body; title long but states finding.
top_changes: Reconcile hit-rate numbers in lede and so-what; state once which pool the headline refers to; say day-3 is directional only (gap 25 points [-14,58]); put repeat-receiver overlap in one clause beside the number.

Collapse 'The test' into one 5-row robustness table (plain, ridge, without Nacua, route-mix adjusted, QB-adjusted); move yards per route run, catch rate over expected, QB model, Holm/shuffle p to appendix; keep one sentence on price lead.

Rewrite 'Why it matters' as real motivation (why WR/TE separation is hard to scout, why a cut metric is plausible, clubs already pay 14% earlier, first class with 10 Hz Combine tracking). Delete 'same code ... frozen and hashed' from 'The metric'; give coach definition: Break G is how hard a receiver drives into the ground in the second around his cut.
judge-writeup.suggested_title: Combine Cuts Don't Predict NFL Separation for Receivers. Last Season's Separation Does.

per_figure.note: Hero. Drill-vs-game paths for same players/route family in common frame with metric readouts and six-player interval strip. Readouts ~8-9 pt, figure tall; Break G in g vs sd in titles; forecast-error intervals uninformative.

Clear, base rate, Wilson intervals, n shown, named players. Puka Nacua label overlaps a point, Washington clipped; base rate 40% in both pools; panel A somewhat circular; same player can appear twice.
Reliability, transfer with null band and ceiling, per-player slopes. Panel 3 crowded caterpillar; panels 1 and 2 carry the message.
Panel A robustness forest good. Panel B labels collide; diamond (~14%) vs dot (~10%) easy to misread; secondary axis unclear; purple bars not intervals.

top_changes: Make Fig 1 work at column width: 4 players or 2x3 grid, readouts at least 10 pt, one scale (g and sd), colour path by acceleration through the 1.0 s window; drop forecast-error strip or replace with drill-vs-NFL Break G dumbbell.

Declutter Fig 4B: offset labels with leaders, print numeric Break G price and value next to diamond and dot matching text (14% [5,23]; dot 10%), drop or explain secondary axis, or reduce to 3-row dumbbell.
Cut Fig 3 panel 3 or replace with small multiples of 3-4 players; fix Fig 2 label collisions; show 4/7 vs 2/5 as counts without interval emphasis.
